thread:
sarah_support: FYI AcmeCorp reporting intermittent 401s when streaming. They say it fails immediately with 401 and no chunks. Request-id: req_9f3b2c. They sent a curl, pasted below.

jess_acme: ```
curl -i \
  -H 'Authorization: Token abc123' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams'
```

sarah_support: thanks. two quick asks: 1) can you rerun with verbose headers (-D -) so we get raw response headers? 2) please use a bearer token header (Authorization: Bearer <token>) — our auth layer expects bearer.

daniel_se: Also try --http1.1 --no-buffer and remove any --compressed flags. Proxies sometimes terminate chunked streaming early. Example we ask them to run: 

```
curl --http1.1 --no-buffer -v -D- \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REPLACE_TOKEN>" \
  -H "User-Agent: AcmeStreamTester/1.0" \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?topic=alerts'
```

ops_infra: if they're behind a corporate proxy it's worth trying with `-H "Connection: keep-alive"` and `--raw` to avoid libcurl decoding. Also ask them to capture a --trace-ascii file so we can see TLS / proxy CONNECT details.

jess_acme: ran the suggested curl, attaching top output: 

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Server: redwood-inference
Date: Tue, 19 Nov 2030 14:12:03 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 85
X-Request-Id: req_9f3b2c
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Redwood"

{"error":"invalid_token","message":"token expired"}
```

sarah_support: good — token expired is helpful. Can you confirm the token you used is fresh (rotate and try a new one)? Also please run the curl again with these exact flags so we can collect a debug bundle: 

```
# produce headers + trace to files (mask tokens before sending)
curl --http1.1 --no-buffer -v -D response_headers.txt \
  --trace-ascii curl_trace.txt \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <NEW_TOKEN>" \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?topic=alerts' > stream_output.txt 2>&1 || true
```

Please attach response_headers.txt, curl_trace.txt, and stream_output.txt. If they can't attach, paste the top ~40 lines of curl_trace.txt and the response headers. Also include exact local time when you ran it (timezone).

daniel_se: on our side we'll search logs for X-Request-Id req_9f3b2c and time window 2025-11-19T14:10:00Z..2025-11-19T14:15:00Z (please confirm the customer's run time so we match). If we see proxy 502/timeout upstream we'll escalate to infra.

jess_acme: attaching the three files now (see DM). Ran at 2025-11-19T14:12:01Z. Token rotated before retry. New run produced 200 and streamed fine. Old token produced 401.

sarah_support: perfect — that indicates token expiry rather than proxy chunking. I'll close the support ticket with remediation steps (refresh tokens, add token lifetime check in their client). Keeping this thread for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Incident ticket INC-2025-431 opened for log correlation (linked req req_9f3b2c).

ops_infra: flagging: we should add a KB snippet for streaming clients behind corporate proxies (recommended curl flags and trace collection).
